findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
(P) 2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Handle of dispenser was touched to dispense paper towels after handwahsing occurred, and paper towels were used to shut off the manual faucet prior to drying hands. Handwashing technique was discussed. Best practice would be to have paper towels ready prior to beginning handwashing process and use paper towels as a barrier after drying hands to shut off the manual faucet and touch the handle of the paper towel dispenser if additional towels need to be dispensed. Elbows and forearms may also be used to touch the handle to dispense paper towels. Ensure proper handwashing occurs between tasks and prior to food preparation and service.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Ground beef cooked this morning to be used for spaghetti on another day was tightly covered with plastic wrap and aluminum foil in the walk-in cooler. Surface temperature was observed at 110F with internal temperatures ranging from 127F-140F. Meat was cooked and placed in the cooler just prior to inspector’s arrival. Best practices were discussed for rapid chilling of cooked TCS foods. Plastic wrap and foil were removed from 3/4 of the pan to allow for release of steam. Manager was advised to stir the meat and monitor the temperature over time to ensure proper cooling. **Total cooling time is 6hrs: 135F to 70F w/in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below w/in additional 4hrs**  
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods. 
 When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be: (1) Arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing and sanitization. Facility did not have chlorine test kit for verifying concentration of bleach solutions. Foods were without date marks that were opened/portioned the week prior. PIC was unfamiliar with employee health requirements. PIC is new to the position since last summer and still in the process of learning but has a food manager certification. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the follow-up inspection.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Employee health documents could not be located at the time of inspection. Employee health documents were provided and discussed with emphasis on knowledge required by management and staff on reporting illness and time frame for exclusion from food handling depending on reportable symptoms versus being diagnosed with and/or potentially exposed to foodborne pathogens. Reporting agreements were signed by kitchen staff at the time of inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Handles of manual faucet and paper towel dispenser were touched after handwashing was completed to shut off faucet and obtain paper towels for drying hands. Proper technique was discussed. Best practice would be to have paper towels ready prior to beginning handwashing process and use paper towels as a barrier after drying hands to shut off the manual faucet and touch the handle of the paper towel dispenser if additional towels need to be dispensed. Elbows and forearms may also be used to shut off the faucet and touch the handle to dispense paper towels. Ensure proper handwashing occurs between tasks and prior to food preparation and service. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Bleach solutions in sani-buckets were observed at 100ppm (back prep) and 200ppm (front service area). Manufacturer’s directions have a required concentration of 200ppm for prepared solutions. Additional bleach was added to the solution observed at 100ppm to bring concentration to 200ppm. Ensure test strips are used to verify proper concentration of bleach solution at 200ppm as required per label directions. 
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Open gallon of milk and diced ham portions in the walk-in cooler were observed without date marks. Milk was opened the Friday prior, and ham was portioned on Friday as well. Proper date marking was discussed, and foods were dated during inspection. Ensure proper date marking of foods. Educational handout on date marking was provided for reference.
Except as specified in  (E) -(G) of this section, refrigerated, ready to eat TCS food prepared and packaged by a food processing plant shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in  (A). The day the original container is opened in the food establishment shall be counted as Day 1, and the day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Chlorine test kit was not available for checking bleach solutions. Maintain a chlorine test kit at the facility to verify concentration of bleach solutions prepared on-site.
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Low water pressure was present when the cold water was in use at the front service line handwashing sink. Have maintenance work to resolve this issue so adequate pressure is available for both hot and cold running water at the handwashing sink.
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. An employee working at the time of inspection had a certification that expired in August 2022. Manager and employee were advised as to the need for re-certification. Ensure certifications are maintained for staff and certificates are renewed prior to expiration dates. New hires need to complete food handler certifications within 30 days of hiring. Copies of current food handler certifications need to be maintained for staff that are not certified food managers.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ice flap in the ice machine to have black mold on it. Empty the ice machine and wash, rinse and sanitize the ice flap.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the front hand washing sink that is not used often to be slow draining. Repair plumbing so that sink drains appropriately.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed a piece of duct tape on the top of the ice machine which seems to be holding the front panel closed. Remove duct tape and repair panel.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed diced ham in the walk in cooler to have a date mark of 4-13-15 (today is 4-23-15). Ham should only be held for 7 days after opening. Ham was discarded during inspection.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.comment:

750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) Top layer of portioned ham cups are holding at 51F.  They were used immediately and no more than 2 layers of pre portioned cups will be placed in the cold holding line.  If food is held out of temperature there must be a memo of understanding on file stating that food held at room temperature will be discarded after 4 hours. These foods must also be labeled with the time they were removed from cold holding.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. The sanitizing solution for wet wiping cloths used on non food contact surfaces measured at 10ppm chlorine.  The sanitizer was changed so that it is at 100ppm chlorine.
